newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister faces fresh sleaze probe.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister faces fresh sleaze probe.

text.p: A French court is to open an inquiry into allegations that ex-trade minister and Lyon mayor Michel Noir, already convicted of sleaze, received cash from companies in return for political favours, justice sources said on Thursday.

They said the probe into complicity in misuse of corporate funds would open in the Cour de Justice, France's only court allowed to investigate and try offences committed by a serving cabinet minister.

Noir has been accused by his jailed son-in-law Pierre Botton of receiving corporate money through a Panama bank account. An ordinary investigating magistrate has handed over the case to the Cour de Justice, saying the allegations covered the time when Noir was a minister between 1986-88.

Noir, who was a member of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist RPR party, has been twice convicted of corruption for receiving illegal funds from Botton and diverting city funds for his own campaigning when he was mayor of Lyon, France's second-largest city, from 1989 to 1995.
He is appealing against separate suspended jail terms of one year and 18 months. Noir has been recently trying his hand at theatre, performing in a production of Chekhov's "Uncle Vanya".
